macros.name: answerline
macros.doc: If you don’t want the students to just circle the correct choices, you can use the \answerline command to print a line on which the answer should be written (see section 7.6).

macros.name: answerline
macros.doc: If you don’t want the students to just circle the correct choices, you can use the \answerline command to print a line on which the answer should be written (see section 7.6).

macros.name: begingradingrange
macros.doc: You can define a grading range by choosing a name with which to label the range, e.g., “myrange”, and then putting the command \begingradingrange{myrange} at the start of the range and the command \endgradingrange{myrange} at the end of the range.

macros.name: bonuspointformat
macros.doc: The \pointformat command controls the printing of “regular” points (i.e., non-bonus points) and the \bonuspointformat command controls the printing of bonus points (see section 4.6).

macros.name: cancelspace
macros.doc: The document class option cancelspace and the command \cancelspace only affect the optional arguments of of the five solution environments solution, solutionorbox, solutionorlines, solutionordottedlines, and solutionorgrid; they do not affect any \vspace commands that you put into the file.

macros.name: CorrectChoice
macros.doc: The command to define a correct choice is \CorrectChoice, which is used in place of the command \choice.

macros.name: droppoints
macros.doc: \droppoints prints the point value in the right margin, formatted as it is when you give the command \pointsinrightmargin, except that the points appear opposite the last line of the paragraph (or, if the command \droppoints is given between paragraphs, then additional vertical space is left between the paragraphs and the points are printed opposite the blank space).

macros.name: droptotalpoints
macros.doc: \droptotalpoints prints the total points for the current question in the right margin, formatted by default as: Total for Question 2: 25 (Note: The number of points is followed by the argument to the most recently executed \marginpointname command (see section 4.3.5), which by default is empty.)

macros.name: extrafootheight
macros.doc: The \extrafootheight command takes an optional argument to provide a bottom margin on the first page that’s different from that on all other pages.

macros.name: extrafootheight
macros.doc: The \extrafootheight command takes an optional argument to provide a bottom margin on the first page that’s different from that on all other pages.

macros.name: extrawidth
macros.doc: The \extrawidth command takes one argument, and enlarges the width of the printed area by the amount of the argument.

macros.name: fillin
macros.doc: There is a \fillin command that prints underlined empty space for creating “fill in the blank” questions.

macros.name: fillin
macros.doc: There is a \fillin command that prints underlined empty space for creating “fill in the blank” questions.

macros.name: fillwithdottedlines
macros.doc: fills vertical space of height length with dotted horizontal lines that run the length of the current line.

macros.name: fillwithgrid
macros.doc: fills vertical space of height length with a grid that runs the length of the current line.

macros.name: fillwithlines
macros.doc: fills vertical space of height length with horizontal lines that run the length of the current line.

macros.name: firstpagefooter
macros.doc: If you want the footer on the first page to be different from that on the other pages, then you should use the commands \firstpagefooter and \runningfooter, which also take three arguments and affect either the first page or all pages except the first.

macros.name: firstpageheader
macros.doc: If you want the header on the first page to be different from that on the other pages, then you should use the commands \firstpageheader and \runningheader, which also take three arguments and affect either the first page or all pages except the first.

macros.name: footer
macros.doc: The command \footer{Text 1}{Text 2}{Text 3} puts “Text 1” into the left justified footer, “Text 2” into the centered footer and “Text 3” into the right justified footer on every page.

macros.name: fullwidth
macros.doc: The \fullwidth command prints its argument using the full width of the printed region, temporarily canceling the indentation created by the questions environment (and the parts, subparts, and subsubparts environments, if you’re inside any of those).

macros.name: gridsize
macros.doc: The period of the grid is \gridsize (both horizontally and vertically).

macros.name: header
macros.doc: The command \header{Text 1}{Text 2}{Text 3} puts “Text 1” into the left justified header, “Text 2” into the centered header, and “Text 3” into the right justified header on every page.

macros.name: ifcontinuation
macros.doc: The \ifcontinuation command figures out which text to use by checking whether there is a \question command appearing on the page before any of the commands \part, \subpart, \subsubpart, \choice, or \CorrectChoice, and this works well for most pages.

macros.name: ifincomplete
macros.doc: expands to ‘Text 1’ if the last question begun on or before the current page continues onto a page after this one, and to ‘Text 2’ otherwise.

macros.name: iflastpage
macros.doc: expands to ‘Text 1’ on the last page and to ‘Text 2’ on all pages before the last.

macros.name: marksnotpoints
macros.doc: If you give the command \marksnotpoints, then the words “point” and “points” will be replaced by the words “mark” and “marks”.

macros.name: nocancelspace
macros.doc: The command \nocancelspace reverts to the default situation (in which the optional arguments are not ignored).

macros.name: noqformat
macros.doc: a \noqformat command, which reverts to the default setup.

macros.name: numcoverpages
macros.doc: The exam document class defines the command \numcoverpages so that it will expand to the number of cover pages in the exam.

macros.name: numpages
macros.doc: The exam document class defines the command \numpages so that it will expand to the number of pages in the exam.

macros.name: numquestions
macros.doc: If you have more than one questions environment (for example, if your exam has several parts, with the questions in each part numbered beginning with “1”), then \numquestions will hold the total number of questions on the exam.

macros.name: oddeven
macros.doc: expands to ‘Text 1’ on odd numbered pages and to ‘Text 2’ on even numbered pages.

macros.doc: You can create a grading table or point table that covers only the questions in a range by using the \partialgradetable or \partialpointtable command.

macros.name: partialpointtable
macros.doc: You can create a grading table or point table that covers only the questions in a range by using the \partialgradetable or \partialpointtable command.

macros.name: pointformat
macros.doc: The \pointformat command controls the printing of “regular” points (i.e., non-bonus points) and the \bonuspointformat command controls the printing of bonus points (see section 4.6).

macros.name: pointsinmargin
macros.doc: If you give the command \pointsinmargin, then the points are printed right justified in the left margin, with the right edge a distance of \marginpointssep from the left edge of the text area.

macros.name: pointsonpage
macros.doc: If you use the document class option addpoints (as in \documentclass[addpoints]{exam}) or give the command \addpoints (see section 3.1), then you can use the \pointsonpage command. This command takes one argument, which must be the number of a page of the exam, and it prints the total number of points for all the questions, parts, subparts, and subsubparts on that page.

macros.name: runningheader
macros.doc: If you want the header on the first page to be different from that on the other pages, then you should use the commands \firstpageheader and \runningheader, which also take three arguments and affect either the first page or all pages except the first.

macros.name: SolutionEmphasis
macros.doc: You can change the appearance of the text of the solution with the \SolutionEmphasis command.

macros.name: solutionsreseteqcounter
macros.doc: If you give the command \solutionsreseteqcounter then every time you begin one of the solution environments, the equation counter will be reset to zero (so that the first equation environment in the solution will be number 1), and when you end that solution environment the equation counter will be restored to whatever it was before the solution environment.

macros.name: solutiontitle
macros.doc: The word “Solution:” that you see at the beginning of the solutions printed by the solution, solutionorbox, solutionorlines, and solutionordottedlines environments can be changed by redefining the command \solutiontitle.

macros.name: titledquestion
macros.doc: The \titledquestion command (see section 4.5.1) allows you to assign a title to a question, and to have the question title replace the question number in a grading table or point table indexed by question number (see sections 9.1 and 9.2).

macros.name: titledquestion
macros.doc: The \titledquestion command (see section 4.5.1) allows you to assign a title to a question, and to have the question title replace the question number in a grading table or point table indexed by question number (see sections 9.1 and 9.2).

macros.name: uplevel
macros.doc: The \uplevel command prints its argument using the indentation in effect before you entered the current innermost environment.

envs.name: coverpages
envs.doc: There is a coverpages environment that allows you to have one or more pages before page 1 of the exam.

envs.name: solutionorbox
envs.doc: By default, the solution is printed in a box whose width equals that of the text of the current question (or part, or subpart, or subsubpart).
